::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the slides at Part 2](../../slides/full.html#/part-2-the-claim-and-its-estimand){target="_blank"} in their own tab, or follow them on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The claim is about countries in years while the surveys hold respondents, so the analysis rests on a panel of country-years, built by averaging the answers of each country in each year, and on models for such a panel. This stage downloads the sixteen Eurobarometer files and turns them into the panel with the scripts of the IDE workspace, writes the estimand statement and the causal graph, and reproduces a recorded result. It takes about six and three quarter hours with the download and the build, and about five without them.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" icon=false}
**The licence of the files.** The Eurobarometer files come under the terms of use of GESIS, which forbid passing them on, publishing anything about individual respondents, and processing them with an AI assistant. They stay on your own machine, out of every repository and out of any session that an AI assistant can read. The panel that the IDE workspace ships is an aggregate, to which none of these restrictions applies.
:::

## 1. The Eurobarometer files

[Download the Eurobarometer files](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-gesis){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Register with GESIS, which is free and immediate, and download the Stata file of each of the sixteen studies, about half a gigabyte in all, by the steps that [the GESIS archive](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-gesis) in the module on data sources takes screen by screen. Read what the terms of use allow and what they forbid.

## 2. Building the analysis file

[Open Building the analysis file](../../companion/data-management.qmd#sec-europeanisation){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Run the first script of the IDE workspace on your sixteen files and read the report that it prints. Then work through the second, which reproduces the country-year panel.

## 7. Task 3 – The reproduction

**On the slides, then in your report**, Task 3 of `index.qmd`.

[Open the slides at Part 3](../../slides/full.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the webR workspace at Task 3](../../lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

Read the opening slides of Part 3, on the instruction of Task 2 of the SCORE robustness study [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness]. Then reproduce one of the three analyses in the chunk of its analyst, `fit-corrected` for C6HJR, `fit-kqxue` for KQXUE or `fit-018ol` for 018OL, reading each line as you run it, until the value on record comes back to the third decimal.

## 8. The models of a panel

[Open Panel data at section 2](../../companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-ols){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Work from [The linear model](../../companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-ols) to [Standard errors with few clusters](../../companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-inference).

**Shortcuts.** Without a GESIS account, or without the time and the disk space that the download takes, skip the download and read the data-management module without running it, since the module quotes what the scripts print and the panel of the IDE workspace is the one that the scripts rebuild. If you have drawn causal graphs for panel data before, read only [the limits of fixed effects](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-growth) in the graph module. If you have fitted regressions with controls before, skip the linear model.
